text:
jordan: Heads up — p95 spiked after the v3.1 rollout, started ~02:10 UTC. Not across all hosts, small cohort looks bad
maya: saw the alert, pulling traces now. interestingly kernel selection time increased on the bad hosts
sam: was there a tokenizer tweak in v3.1?
jordan: yep — changed whitespace normalization + added more explicit EOS tokens. median seq_len jumped ~48 -> ~86 in prod samples
elaine: that could trigger the batching heuristic to favor different kernel paths and smaller batches. also seeing KV cache miss rate increase on those hosts
perf-bot: perf summary: p50 60ms->68ms, p95 210ms->340ms, throughput -12% on affected machines
ops-bot: tagged hosts with label noisy-tenant-42 as suspects and put a temporary routing rule to avoid them for critical routes :white_check_mark:
maya: quick profiler snapshot (remote):
```
kv_cache.hit_rate: 0.62 -> 0.38
seq_len.median: 48 -> 86
batcher.avg_batch_size: 8.0 -> 3.2
kernel_selection.latency_ms: 1.8 -> 6.4
chosen_kernel: matmul_opt -> generic_fallback
cpu_steal_pct: 0.7 -> 4.9
```
sam: so three things compounding: tokenizer produces longer sequences -> smaller batches -> different kernel chosen; KV cache keys shift (prefix change) -> fewer cache hits; and noisy tenant causing CPU steal on same hosts
jordan: logs show a burst of small requests from tenant 42 at same window, likely noisy neighbor effect. we saw elevated context-switches too
elaine: short-term mitigation: force fallback to matmul_opt for this model on suspected hosts and increase kv cache retention for prefix keys. longer term: we need batching heuristic to consider seq_len distribution change smoothly
maya: repro plan: roll v3.1 in staging with sampled traffic from tenant 42 and run `python infra/tools/kvprof.py --host <host> --duration 300` to capture KV traces
jordan: running the staging replay now. if we can reproduce, we should either patch tokenizer or add a tokenizer-compatibility toggle in rollout config
sam: i'm comfortable doing a quick rollback of the tokenizer change if repro matches. would prefer adding an automatic kernel fallback first so customer impact is minimized
elaine: I'll open a config PR to pin kernel selection for this model and a small change to increase batcher's lookback window from 30s -> 90s (so it sees the new seq_len distribution before switching kernels)
perf-bot: can someone post the flamegraph link?
maya: flame uploaded: https://internal-s3/redwood/perf/1767777777/v3.1-flame.html
ops-bot: routing rule applied to remove noisy-tenant-42 from production critical pool (temporary).
jordan: assigned @sam for rollback if needed, @elaine for kernel policy PR, @maya for repro + profiler capture. ETA 2h for first mitigation steps
sam: quick command I ran in staging to check batcher metrics: `ddtrace exec -- python -m tickets/replay --model v3.1 --rate 100` produced avg batch size 3.1 and kernel switch logs
elaine: FYI adding a simple policy: if median_seq_len increases >30% within 5m, delay kernel switch by 5m and force a soft-fallback kernel. we'll stage that change in canary
jordan: nice. also need an alert when kv_cache.hit_rate drops >15% for a model after rollout, can someone add?
maya: will add alert rule and the profiler dashboard panel for kv prefixes.
ops-bot: incident note created: INC-2026-0421 (performance regression v3.1)
jordan: plan to monitor for 1h after routing rule + kernel pin. if p95 not back near baseline we'll rollback tokenizer change. thanks all :pray:
perf-bot: closing loop: p95 target for mitigation check in 60min.
